issues.problem: 'A perfect gate over v3w, tail and sw still left X1 close-following about 10 % above no control' is in none of the verified material, and I found no source for it: not in round_2_result.md, not in docs/research/round2/report/, not in any scratchpad analysis. The recommendation ('report the oracle result as a measured ceiling') and its cons ('the few percent the oracle shows') rest on it. My own check (critic/oracle.out) shows the result depends on how the gate is defined. An arm-level gate (per seed, the lowest of the v3w, tail and sw arm means) gives 9.6 % more than nc [0.6, 19.3], which matches 'about 10 %'. A per-learner gate (per seed, the lowest of w_i, t_i, s_i, then the mean over i) gives 0.9 % more [-5.9, +11.5], not shown to differ from nc. Both are in-sample upper bounds.
issues.fix: Remove the number, or define the gate and have it verified. If kept, report both definitions and their CIs. Reword the recommendation: 'An arm-level oracle stays above no control, but a per-learner oracle does not; this data does not rule switching out for X1 close-following.' Drop 'measured ceiling'.

issues.problem: The draft suggests X1-like double slowdowns in training 'as a cheap add-on'. It leaves out that round 2 already trained this. Candidate 'rep' 'carries X1's two-event structure in training' (round_2_result.md l.450) and was not shown better than v3w at validation: X1 TTC +0.2 [-3.1, +4.2], X1 delay -0.4 [-1.6, +1.0] (l.115). Four other trained changes were not shown better either: annealing, the gate hold, the 0.1-s braking charge (1D: X1 TTC +4.4 [-0.1, 6.5]) and the look-ahead inputs (§7.1 l.421). The severity-aware term in reading 1 is close to 1D's braking charge.
issues.fix: Cite round 2's five trained changes and their validation results. Replace 'reasonable as a cheap add-on' with 'already tried as rep; X1 close-following not shown to differ from v3w'. Before proposing a severity or braking term, say how it differs from 1D's 0.1-s braking charge.

issues.where: Author question: were X1/X2 trained together or separately (whole draft)
issues.problem: The draft never answers this. §2 only places the cells against the training draw.
issues.fix: Add an explicit answer. Neither cell was a training condition: each of v3w's 5 learners was trained on the 'random' single-slowdown draw. X2 lies inside the draw, with its duration at the bound; X1's second event lies outside. rep added X1's two-event structure and was not shown better (round_2_result.md l.115, l.450). Only the rules were tuned per cell: 3E-X1 and 3E-X2 were tuned separately by CMA-ES, and neither search converged (l.9, l.12). 3E-T was tuned under the training draw (l.8).

issues.problem: Plan B proposes pre-registering a new comparison on X1/X2 on this plant without disclosing the recorded closures. Under V466 (round_2_result.md §7.3), the DRL claim against tuned rules is closed in X2 on this plant: 'no further DRL training, tuning, plant change or seed round is run in X2 on this plant'. X1 closed under confirmatory 3's [A3] (V395), and round 2 was already its third test on plant_c3. A new X1 test would be the fourth (forking paths). Also, V462(4) and round_2_result.md l.396 label the band and condition T (the random draw) 'outside the plant's stated intended use', and the operating-map analyst noted the same applies at least as much to 3,500 and 7,000. Three of the five 'dense settings' (5,500, 6,000, 7,000) that carry the Plan B evidence are such rows. §7(b) lists V462(4) as 'Open', but the report already answers it.

issues.where: §7(a) line 380 ('What the evidence already supports…') and reading 3, line 378
issues.problem: 'act … in recovery traffic' and 'gap choice … during recovery' bring back the D8 reading the verifier corrected. Relative to nc, the excess is similar in hold (20.0 % [-4.8, 25.4]), after (18.1 % [9.6, 25.3]) and rest (23.4 % [11.4, 31.1]). Per second it is +0.20, +0.25 and +0.27 TTC-s/s. 'Rest' leads only because it lasts 720 s. 'Not on a whole-network count' does not follow either: the network count shows the excess (+224 [119, 328]). The cancellation argument holds for sev3, not for ttc_net. A term aimed only at 4a and edge 3 could give back the gains on ramp 2 (-113) and the rest of the network (-73), and at merge 1 in X2.
issues.fix: Replace with: 'from the first slowdown on, on 4a and edge 3, while keeping the ramp-2 and merge-1 gains'. Drop 'recovery' from reading 3.

issues.where: §7(a) as a whole: author's 'without losing delay or X2'
issues.problem: The draft gives no guard for delay or for X2. The verified X2 mechanism is not linked to the recommendation: v3w's parity with nc in X2 rests on removing nc's merge-1 queue (E30 -287.5 [-379.0, -201.9]), which offsets +216.8 [159.0, 276.2] elsewhere. A change that weakens that removal would lose X2. The delay risk in 'cons' cites decisions vm3, but that links short-gap share to close-following among rules, not close-following to delay. Also, X2 is closed (V466), so it can serve only as a report-only guard.
issues.fix: Add guards fixed in advance: delay against v3w within the 2 % limit, X2 ttc_net and E30 not worse than v3w's, and X2 read report-only under V466. Mark the delay-cost sentence '(my inference)'.
